action: Closing call to adult ed coordinator; called Howard Liu about pipeline connection; sold one school vehicle on Facebook Marketplace and Auto Row; followed up with Mark Thompson on board vote timeline and grant contact
narrative: Frank sold the lower-value school vehicle — a 2016 Honda Civic used for student lessons — through a combination of Facebook Marketplace and a quick offer from an Auto Row used lot, netting roughly $4,500 after the outstanding insurance cancellation. The adult ed coordinator, Sandra Reyes, returned his closing call and said exactly what Frank feared: she appreciates the curriculum document and Mark Thompson's endorsement, but the spring catalog decisions aren't made until the district committee meets in three weeks — she can't give him a yes today, but she hasn't said no. Howard Liu's call turned out to be relevant: Howard had heard through Mark that Frank was developing an AV literacy curriculum and wanted to know if Frank might be interested in doing a single-session workshop for his parts store employees, whose work increasingly involves EV diagnostics. It is not steady income, but it is a real ask from a real person. Mark confirmed the board has not yet voted but the secretary said a formal decision is expected within the next two ticks.
